date.source: The page's own header: Live on Pay Per View, Tropicana Field, St. Petersburg, Florida, Sunday night 8 February 2004. The fed's own pay-per-view archive lists it as Tainted Love 2004 on 8 February 2004.

notes: The pay-per-view transcript with nine matches: the main event, a Three Stages of Hell Match for the Universal Title between James Kimson and Asis, ends with Sovereign's return and Asis taking the title; Damon O'Halloran takes the United Title from Matt Hunt in a Ladder Match; The Brotherhood of X keep the Tag Team Titles because a disqualification cannot move them.

evidence.note: The pay-per-view transcript with nine matches: the main event, a Three Stages of Hell Match for the Universal Title between James Kimson and Asis, ends with Sovereign's return and Asis taking the title; Damon O'Halloran takes the United Title from Matt Hunt in a Ladder Match; The Brotherhood of X keep the Tag Team Titles because a disqualification cannot move them.

matches.note: Non-Title. The referee called for the bell on Psymon's full nelson after a Ganso Bomb left Kira motionless; the page announces no winner.
Non-Title. The page's own line: Winners, Kin Sakoda and Yoshii Tanaka; Larry Spades's leg drop meant for Kin kicked his brother in the face, and Kin fell onto Greg and pinned him.
Non-Title. The fight began backstage; Ethan Coles won with a modified Golden Handshake through a table, and the referee handed him the belt he bought the week before.

matches.stipulation: Six Man Tag Team Match (two out of three falls)
matches.note: Tag Team Titles, The Brotherhood of X(c). Eric Knight and Deacon of St. Violence officiated. Shaft-Man took the first fall with a small package; The Brotherhood of X were disqualified in the second for outside interference, which gave the challengers the match, but the ring announcer ruled that a title cannot change hands on a disqualification, so The Brotherhood of X kept the titles.
Non-Title. Shocka was first given the fall after grabbing the ropes; the referee reversed that on the replay and the match went on, ending with Xander's Chaos Reigns from the top rope.
Non-Title. Big Daddy Dreamer made Tyler Davidson tap out to the Dreamer Crossface.
Non-Title. The HeartBreak Chick pinned Thug roC with the Kiss of Death after an earlier three count was waved off.
United Title, Matt Hunt(c). Damon O'Halloran, a tazer and a ladder in play, climbed to the belt and grabbed it; the referee called the bell and laid the belt across him while Hunt lay unmoving.

Universal Title, James Kimson(c). Asis won the first fall (standard) and Kimson the second (street fight); Sovereign attacked Kimson in the third (Last Man Standing), and Asis got to his feet for the ten count to take the title.

name: Legends (7 April 2004)

date.source: The page's own header: Live on Tru-TV, Chapel Hill, North Carolina, the Dean Smith Center, Wednesday night 7 April 2004. The page gives no episode number.

notes: The weekly Legends of the week before Unbreakable: Tyler Davidson announces the Board of Directors' funding cut and a list of released wrestlers, Asis beats Tyler Davidson in a No Holds Barred Match for the Universal Title, and Xander takes the title from him immediately afterwards.

evidence.note: The weekly Legends of the week before Unbreakable: Tyler Davidson announces the Board of Directors' funding cut and a list of released wrestlers, Asis beats Tyler Davidson in a No Holds Barred Match for the Universal Title, and Xander takes the title from him immediately afterwards.

matches.note: Universal Title, Asis(c). The company's executive managed Tyler Davidson for the night and hit Asis with the title belt; Asis retained, pinning Tyler Davidson on the floor after the Red Death.

Universal Title, Asis(c). Xander took a title shot that the executive had promised him earlier in the night, on the spot, and won with Chaos Reigns after Asis gored himself through the eVolution logo screen.

name: Unbreakable 2004

date.source: The fed's shut-down news calls the show Unbreakable and says it was held the night before the news was posted; the Legends of 7 April 2004 names Unbreakable as the next pay-per-view, and the fed's own pay-per-view page, as it stood on 28 April 2004, bills the next pay-per-view for Sunday 11 April 2004 at the Charlotte Coliseum. The date and venue are read from that page; no page states them beside the name Unbreakable.

notes: The fed's last show, not televised: three matches, with the results given in its shut-down news. The Universal Title match ended when Asis powerbombed Xander through an exploding table and Xander was removed from the match; the Board of Directors voted to close the federation after it.

Xander(c), newly champion. Asis powerbombed Xander off the cage and through an exploding table outside it, and Xander was removed from the match; the news item gives the result as Asis def. Malcolm King and Xander.
